question: For each of the 50 states, plus the D.C. mayor and the Puerto Rico governor, answered as one set: what are the qualifications to hold the office (minimum age, years of state residency or citizenship, U.S. citizenship and for how long, being a qualified elector or registered voter, any bar for felony conviction, other offices held or impeachment), and on what date each is tested (filing, election or taking office)? Cite the constitutional or statutory provision and mark anything not found as UNKNOWN.
requestedBy: A corrupt life in power playtest thread, filed by the research intake thread

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Governor rows exist for MN, MO, NE and OH only.
It gives terms and dates, not qualifications.
100 governor rows for ten states (NC, ND, NM, NY, OH, OK, OR, PA, RI, SC); the other 42 jurisdictions have none, and the rows need re-verification against current text.

title: What it takes to be eligible for governor, in every state
usableAnswer: A 52-row table: jurisdiction; minimum age; state residency and its length; citizenship; elector or registration requirement; other bars; the date each is tested; citations; and an evidence status per field.
whyItMatters: Filing for governor checks no qualification at all: src/simulation/nationwide-world/state-executive-candidacy-packs.ts marks minimumAge, residency and termYears as unknownRule for every state without a pack (around line 231 at main 5c971245), and fileForStateExecutiveOffice checks none of them. In play, a 40-year-old started in Nome, Alaska filed and was sworn in as governor, while the same life was refused a state House seat for lacking a year's recorded district residence. The qualification corpus (data/source/state-office-qualifications/corpus.json) holds governor rows for only Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska and Ohio, and docs/research/31D-recovered-qualifications.tsv has governor rows for ten more (NC, ND, NM, NY, OH, OK, OR, PA, RI, SC), none of them wired into governor filing. The Puerto Rico answer (puerto-rico-government-and-municipios) already gives that governor's rules.
